To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Hsp27 interacts with β-catenin, and that this interaction may have prognostic significance in breast cancer.
Hsp27 and β-catenins are coexpressed in breast cancer patients and that β-catenin can bind to Hsp27.
the cadherin-catenin protein system is functionally connected to the heat shock protein response in breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional interactions between the cadherin and catenin proteins and the heat shock proteins, with a focus on the prognostic importance of the expression of these proteins in breast cancer.
the molecular interactions of HSP with cadherin–β-catenin cell adhesion system and the prognostic relevance of the coexpression of HSP with the adhesion molecules.
the functional interactions between the cell adhesion system and the HSP response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Hsp27 and β-catenins are prognostic biomarkers in breast cancer, and they are functionally linked to one another.
Hsp27 and β-catenins may interact in breast cancer cells and that this may influence the prognosis of the patients.

the HSP and the cadherins–catenins have a complex and multifaceted relationship, and that the HSP may be involved in the regulation of cadherin expression, the regulation of the cytoskeletal proteins that interact with the cadherins, the regulation of β-catenins and the regulation of the transcriptional factors that regulate cadherin gene expression and β-catenins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Hsp27 and HSF1 are part of a network of proteins that regulate the cadherin-catenin system and thereby influence tumor cell survival.
Hsp27 and HSF1 are involved in the molecular pathways that regulate β-catenin function and that the cadherin-catenin system may be a target for HSPs.

the cadherin- and catenin-related proteins interact with the heat shock proteins, which are known to have an important role in the regulation of cell survival, and the cadherins and catenins are prognostic markers of clinical importance in breast cancer patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat shock response may be involved in the regulation of the cell adhesion system in cancer.
β-catenin may be an important player in the HSP response in breast cancer.
the heat shock proteins and the cell adhesion molecules are linked in the biology of breast cancer.
